blocks.prompt: 12 If \(f(a + x) + f(a - x) = 0\), show that \(\int_{0}^{2a} f(x)\,dx = 0\).
blocks.explanation:
A proof: \(f\) is 'odd about \(x = a\)', the midpoint of \([0, 2a]\).
Property IV replaces \(x\) by \(2a - x\); the condition (with \(x\) replaced by \(a - x\)) says \(f(2a - x) = -f(x)\).
So the integral equals its own negative.
steps:
Given: \(f(a + x) + f(a - x) = 0\) for all \(x\).
To prove: \(\int_{0}^{2a} f(x)\,dx = 0\).
Method: Property IV \(\int_0^{2a} f(x)\,dx = \int_0^{2a} f(2a - x)\,dx\).

Rewrite the condition
\[x \to a - x:\ f(2a - x) + f(x) = 0\]
\[f(2a - x) = -f(x)\]
Why: \(a + (a - x) = 2a - x\) and \(a - (a - x) = x\); the condition holds for every \(x\), so also for \(a - x\).

Apply Property IV
\[I = \int_{0}^{2a} f(x)\,dx = \int_{0}^{2a} f(2a - x)\,dx\]
\[= -\int_{0}^{2a} f(x)\,dx = -I\]
Why: \(0 + 2a - x = 2a - x\), then the rewritten condition.

Solve
\[I = -I \Rightarrow 2I = 0 \Rightarrow I = 0\]
Why: the only number equal to its own negative is 0.

Check with an example
\[a = 3,\quad f(x) = (x - 3)^3\]
\[\int_{0}^{6} (x - 3)^3\,dx = \left[\dfrac{(x - 3)^4}{4}\right]_{0}^{6}\]
\[= \dfrac{81}{4} - \dfrac{81}{4} = 0 \;\checkmark\]
Why: \(f(3 + x) + f(3 - x) = x^3 - x^3 = 0\), and the integral is 0.
